data.hypothesis: The selected pointer-hoisted OpenMP-SIMD parent measured 0.083408 s; a prior valid scalar formulation measured 0.453027 s, while the best recorded SIMD candidate measured 0.079254 s. This contrasting experiment removes the SIMD directive and gives the kernel output pointer a guarded no-alias qualifier, testing whether the frozen compiler can vectorize the contiguous x loop from alias information alone. The interior row start and arithmetic are unchanged; no speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: For this kernel, distinguish explicit OpenMP SIMD from compiler auto-vectorization; keep row bounds and the x0 offset unchanged when comparing them.
memory_lessons.claim: Recorded valid candidates range from 0.453027 s for a scalar formulation to 0.079254 s for the fastest SIMD formulation, but the measurements alone do not establish which compiler transformation caused the difference.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure a no-SIMD loop with guarded output no-alias information under the same official settings.

data.notes: Retains the selected parent eba63a097bf34ec2 as the AB-MCTS parent and imports no integration sources. This is a source-only candidate; correctness and performance remain for the controller to validate and measure. The no-alias qualifier is applied only to the output pointer and only for compilers identified by the guarded macros; the fallback remains ordinary C++.
transformations: Guard a compiler-specific output no-alias qualifier with GNU/Clang/MSVC compiler macros and leave it empty for other compilers.
Remove the OpenMP SIMD directive to test ordinary compiler auto-vectorization while keeping the canonical contiguous x loop.
Preserve row pointers beginning at x0, stencil arithmetic, spatial bounds, timestep parity, and all interfaces.
Do not change compiler flags, threading, or spatial or temporal blocking.
